guarantees.claim: unused_otp_sigs is always the XOR of root_key_i.creator_seed, creator_seed_valid, owner_seed, owner_seed_valid.
root_key_valid_q is the double-synchronized version of (root_key_i.creator_root_key_share0_valid && root_key_i.creator_root_key_share1_valid).
guarantees.cond: on every clock edge when rst_ni is de-asserted

guarantees.claim: cdi_cnt is assigned cnt[CdiWidth-1:0] when op_req is true, otherwise '0.

assumptions.claim: root_key_i.creator_root_key_share0_valid and share1_valid are flopped outputs from OTP_CTRL and only transition from 0 to 1 once, so AND before synchronizer is glitch-free.
assumptions.risk: If the signals contain glitches or multiple transitions, the synchronizer may sample a false high and set root_key_valid_q incorrectly.

assumptions.claim: cnt has a bit width of at least CdiWidth, so that cnt[CdiWidth-1:0] is a legal bit-select.
assumptions.risk: If CdiWidth exceeds the width of cnt, the select is out of range and cdi_cnt will be X, breaking the function.

uncertain_points.claim: Seeds (creator_seed, owner_seed) are XORed into unused_otp_sigs, which is deliberately unused; this may leak secret values through power/EM side channels if the signal toggles.
uncertain_points.risk: Potential information leakage of root seeds via dynamic power or electromagnetic radiation from the unused_otp_sigs net.

uncertain_points.claim: CdiWidth is a parameter that may be set larger than the actual width of cnt, causing an out-of-range bit-select on cdi_cnt.
uncertain_points.risk: cdi_cnt would be X during op_req, leading to incorrect CDI value propagation and possible functional failure.
